summary: Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under several traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and U Sajjanasāra, and earned his PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under the supervision of J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014).

Sibani Das Gupta is an Indology scholar. She studied at the University of Dhaka, under Rajendra Chandra Hazra, and completed her doctorate at the University of Calcutta in 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibaraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sibnath Sarma as doctoral supervisor, along with teachers D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah, and was attested as Lecturer at North Lakhimpur College (2012).

Sicheng Liang (1901–1972) was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at Beijing Huiwen Middle School, Tsinghua University (~1915–1923), and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (~1924–1927), and later held a post at Peking University.

Sidney Lee (1859–1926) was a historian. He was educated at the City of London School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882), and later served on the faculty at Queen Mary University of London (~1913–1924).

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth at Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Tübingen (PhD 1867), later becoming an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) was an Indologist who studied at Vienna (Dr. phil. 1949), Paris, and Stockholm (Habilitation ~1961–1963). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Kiel University, and served as professor at Stockholm University (1968–1990).

Siglinde Dietz (b. 1944) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn in 1980 under Michael Hahn and was affiliated with the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
Signe Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. She holds a post as Professor at the University of Missouri.
Signe Howell (1942–2025) studied at SOAS University of London (~1970–1973) and the University of Oxford (~1974–1980). In 1989, she was appointed Professor at the University of Oslo.

Silvia Luraghi (b. 1958) is a linguist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Turin (~1977–1982) and held academic posts at the University of Turin (~1993–1998), Università degli Studi Roma Tre (~1998–1999), and the University of Pavia (~1999).

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he taught at Naples "L'Orientale," Sapienza, and Naples Federico II, and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2001–2023).

Simo Knuuttila (1946–2022) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. After studying at the University of Helsinki (1976), he served there as Professor (~1981–2014) and held a post at the Academy of Finland (1994–2004).

Simo Parpola (b. 1943), a scholar of linguistics and archaeology, earned his PhD at Helsinki (1968) and also studied at Pontifical Biblical Institute and the British Museum. He held posts at Heidelberg, Chicago, and Helsinki (appointed professor 1978).

Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held appointments at Durham University as a Tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as a Lecturer in Philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Simon Winant is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).
Siniruddha Dash is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras from 2000 to 2014 and became director of the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation in 2020.

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, Harvard, and London under Frank Raymond Allchin. He served as Director General of the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy who studied under Debabrata SenSharma. He has held positions as Professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Zhihua Yao and completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.
